Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the United Arab Emirates' reply. The umpires and players have made their way out to the middle. Muhammad Waseem and Aryansh Sharma will open the innings for the United Arab Emirates. Tim Southee has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, this first T20I is set up nicely with both sides being pretty pleased with the proceedings. The United Arab Emirates would have liked to keep New Zealand under 150 but this is a total they will fancy themselves to chase. As far as New Zealand are concerned, they will go into their bowling effort with momentum behind them and they do have the resources to defend this total. We shall find out how the chase unfolds when we return.

Basil Hameed is in for a chat. He starts by thanking the almighty and says that they pulled things back really well and it is now up to the batters to take them over the line. Adds that his idea was to bowl at the stumps and not give any room to the batters. Says that the wicket should get better in the second innings and it is important for the openers to see off the early difficulty. Ends by saying that they are excited to play against a quality side like New Zealand and he hopes to win the game with the bat.

For the United Arab Emirates, Junaid Siddique got them off to the best possible start with a wicket on the first delivery of the game. They were unable to contain Tim Seifert who was blazing away but pulled things back nicely after the Powerplay. Basil Hameed wasted no time and dealt twin blows in his first over. Playing in his maiden T20I game, Mohammed Faraazuddin chipped in as well to put New Zealand in further trouble. The UAE bowlers bowled disciplined lines and lengths for most parts of their bowling effort to keep New Zealand in check. That said, Muhammad Waseem will be disappointed with how things panned out in the last few overs.

New Zealand finish on a high and end up with a competitive total on the board! After being inserted into bat by Muhammad Waseem, New Zealand lost Chad Bowes early but Tim Seifert was unperturbed by it and scored at a brisk pace in the Powerplay. In no time, the visitors slipped from 51-1 to 64-4 and found themselves struggling against the spinners. James Neesham then began resurrecting the innings and found able allies in Mark Chapman and Cole McConchie. Just when Neesham was starting to get a move on, he was dismissed which pegged back New Zealand big time. At 109-6, Cole McConchie joined hands with Rachin Ravindra and strung an unbeaten 46-run partnership to take New Zealand over 150.

A couple of runs to end and New Zealand finish with a bit of a flourish. Slower and into the pitch outside off. Cole McConchie steps out and has to reach for it a bit before slapping it down to long off. The batters push hard for two and get it in the end. New Zealand finish with 155/6!

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Whoa, a dream start for Junaid Siddique and the United Arab Emirates! Siddique comes from over the wicket and hits the hard length, just outside off, Chad Bowes hangs on the back foot and goes for the pull without much foot movement. Ends up getting an under edge that travels low behind the wicket. Aryansh Sharma does extremely well to get down and pouch it inches off the ground. Not a great to the series for Chad Bowes as he departs on a golden duck.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the match to begin! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of United Arab Emirates. It will be the pair of Chad Bowes and Tim Seifert to open the innings for New Zealand. Junaid Siddique has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Tim Southee, the skipper of New Zealand, says that they would have bowled first as well. Reckons that it is a pretty good surface and feels it will remain same throughout 40 overs. Mentions that they have had a few days to acclimatise to the warm conditions. Feels that it is a chance for guys to show what they are capable of.

Muhammad Waseem, the captain of the United Arab Emirates, says that they will bowl first as the pitch looks fresh and will look to restrict them to a low total. Adds that they have to take advantage of the home conditions. Mentions that they have multiple debutants for this game.
New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tim Seifert, Chad Bowes, Dane Cleaver (WK), Mark Chapman, Mitchell Santner, James Neesham, Rachin Ravindra, Cole McConchie, Kyle Jamieson, Tim Southee (C), Benjamin Lister.

United Arab Emirates (Playing XI) - Muhammad Waseem (C), Aryansh Sharma (WK), Vriitya Aravind, Asif Khan, Ansh Tandon, Basil Hameed, Ali Naseer, Aayan Khan, Mohammed Faraazuddin, Junaid Siddique, Zahoor Khan.
TOSS - The coin toss lands in the favour of Muhammad Waseem and the United Arab Emirates have opted to BOWL first.

On the flip side, New Zealand's last T20I assignment in Pakistan ended on level terms, which was a positive result for them considering they lost the first two games. Heading into this series, the visitors will have one eye on the Men's T20I World Cup scheduled to be played in the Caribbean and the USA next year. Like the United Arab Emirates, New Zealand have some fresh faces in their side who will be getting their first taste of international cricket. Tim Southee and Co. do start as favourites, but can they live up to that tag? Or does the United Arab Emirates have an upset in store for us? Stick around to find out, as the toss and team news is not far away.

The hosts, United Arab Emirates, are coming off a home series defeat at the hands of Afghanistan in this format. Under the new leadership of Muhammad Waseem, they are aiming for their first bilateral series win in the T20I format against a Test-playing nation. They have made some tough selection calls for this series, which allows the newcomers to express themselves against a top unit like New Zealand.

Hello and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen, to our coverage of the first T20I between the United Arab Emirates and New Zealand at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium. This three-match T20I series has a history attached, with this being the first bilateral series between these two proud cricketing nations.
... MATCH DAY ...

Folks, history is about to be written as New Zealand will face off against the United Arab Emirates in a bilateral series for the very first time. The two sides are all set to lock horns in a three-match T20I series, with all three T20Is taking place at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium. With the 2024 Men's T20I World Cup starting in just over 9 months, both teams will want to start their preparations for the event through this series. Being ranked in the top eight teams, New Zealand have already qualified for the main event, while the United Arab Emirates will have to take the Qualifier route if they are to make the trip to the Caribbean and the USA. The hosts, United Arab Emirates, will play this series under their new T20I captain, Muhammad Waseem, and he will be hoping to bring some fresh energy to the side. The experienced all-rounder Rohan Mustafa has been left out of the squad, meaning the likes of Aayan Khan, Ali Naseer, and Mohammed Faraazuddin will be expected to fill that void with both bat and ball. In the batting department, Muhammad Waseem, Vriitya Aravind, Asif Khan, and Basil Hameed will have to put their best foot forward against the strong bowling unit of New Zealand. The pace duo of Junaid Siddique and Zahoor Khan will pose a serious threat in home conditions, while they also have the exuberance of youth in the pace department in Muhammad Jawadullah and Sanchit Sharma. On the other hand, New Zealand, the semi-finalists of the 2022 Men's T20I World Cup, will be led by ace pacer Tim Southee. Their batting will have no shortage of firepower with the presence of Tim Seifert, Chad Bowes, and Will Young in the top order. When it comes to the all-rounders, James Neesham, Mark Chapman, and Mitchell Santner stand out, but they also have uncapped Dean Foxcroft, who has been impressive in the New Zealand domestic circuit. The visitors' squad announcement was headlined by the return of Kyle Jamieson after a long injury layoff. Other than him and Southee, Jacob Duffy and Benjamin Lister are the other two seaming options in their ranks. Despite it being an away series for them, this new-look New Zealand does start as favourites to clinch the series. That said, cricket is a funny game, especially in the T20I format, where any team can beat their opponent on any given day. Who will reign supreme in this battle of David and Goliath? We will find out together.
